title: Sign in on a device: confirm
summary: The explicit confirm every device-code sign-in ends with when no license choice or consent step runs (B9): Diceroll on Living room PC is named now that the code resolved, Mara is the account, and 'Sign in on Living room PC?' has equal-size Sign in and Deny. The device waits on 'pending' until she answers.
compare: Always shown on the device-code path when no license choice or consent supplies the explicit step; a scan or a code is never approval (B9, auth-12).
The title names the device the code came from ('Sign in on Living room PC?') and the lede the code and when it was shown, so a person who didn't start it can tell.
Allow and Deny are the same size and both block (Deny outlined); Deny leaves nothing signed in and the device shows it was denied.
The account row is first (who is signing in), with Not you?; on a phone the email wraps, never truncated.
Passport in a landscape window ≥960px (Diceroll's art, icon, developer and device on their own lines); header strip in portrait and on a phone (B8).
No wire change: the device keeps polling 'pending' until the confirm; the design rule is the page.
Round 2 (UX review): Passport as identity.sign-in: the art fills the pane, the identity at its foot (M4).

Round 2 (UX review): M10 (graph note, not a mockup change): the catalog's signInHandoff.confirm ('Choose Continue to {product} on the sign-in page to finish.') must change with I-37 to name this button ('Sign in on <device>').
